appraisal_events.evidence: je tremblais comme un coupable au moment où elle passait ; et quelquefois... je répondais à peine à son salut, ou je la fixais du regard sans la saluer, ni réussir qu'à l'irriter davantage et à faire qu'elle commença en plus à me trouver insolent et mal élevé.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's anxious, involuntary reactions on encountering Mme de Guermantes (trembling, barely acknowledging her greeting, staring without saluting) only irritate her further and lead her to begin judging him as insolent and badly brought up, in contrast to the ordinary passersby whose greetings she tolerates or welcomes.

status_effects.explanation: The passage states plainly that the duchesse comes to regard the narrator as insolent and ill-mannered, a clear negative shift in how he is locally judged.

The narrator is shown as anxious and involuntarily awkward in her presence, unable to control his own reactions, while she finds no relief or escape from herself in him, unlike in the strangers she greets.

ambiguities: The duchesse's growing judgment of the narrator as insolent and ill-mannered is conveyed through the narrator's own retrospective account rather than her direct speech, so the attribution of this judgment to her mind is an inference (free indirect style) rather than a confirmed fact.
